name: Src File Outer Refactoring Audit
query: period_state's Outer Refactoring gate is due. Audit src/beansmeans/period_state.py against the Standards and tell me what to inspect.
context: beansmeans repo, cwd is the project root. The code-compliance skill's baked-in data (scripts/jev_code_compliance_data.json) already exists and is current with Standards/CODE_STANDARDS.md. src/beansmeans/period_state.py has 9 top-level constructs (3 frozen dataclasses, 1 StrEnum, 5 functions).
expected_behavior: Runs uv run E:/work/.agents/skills/code-compliance/scripts/jev_code_compliance.py src/beansmeans/period_state.py --out <matrix.json>, with no --module-kind/--src-criteria/--test-criteria flags

Every construct is classified role=src (a src-kind module always uses the src role, per jev_code_compliance.py's _classify), inferred automatically because the path is not under a tests directory and does not start with test_
Because the full src principle table (131 principles, 16 worked examples) does not fit one 64 KiB request, each construct costs more than one Jev call -- this is expected, not treated as a bug
Runs uv run E:/work/.agents/skills/code-compliance/scripts/jev_code_compliance_report.py against the resulting matrix to render the report
Writes the report to src/beansmeans/period_state.py.jev.compliance-report.{n}.md, incrementing {n} past any existing report for that file rather than overwriting it
Presents the 'Needs inspection' rows to the user as leads to check against real source, not as confirmed defects
Does not edit period_state.py on the strength of the report alone without the user inspecting flagged rows first
success_criteria: The report's construct count matches the file's actual top-level construct count (9)
The report has a Principles section (ID, Term, Sources), a Needs inspection section, and a Full matrix section, in that order
Needs inspection rows are sorted worst-first (highest attention: low score, high confidence, high applicability)
Every principle ID cited in Needs inspection also appears in the Principles legend
The Jev call count reported is at least 2x the construct count (batching, not one call per construct)
